lina: hi everyone, lina here (first day). trying to follow the runtime quickstart on a linux VM but the link step fails referencing libnvrtc. used the devcontainer instructions and mounted /usr/local/cuda.

lina: link error paste:
```
/usr/bin/ld: build/obj/cuda_compilation.o: undefined reference to `nvrtcCreateProgram'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

ben: welcome! :wave: quick checks: inside the container run `ldd build/runtime | grep nvrtc` and `ls /usr/local/cuda-*/lib64 | grep nvrtc`. If it says "not found" you either need the toolkit targets or the libnvrtc package.

anya: we sometimes see this when people install a trimmed driver-only image. If `/usr/local/cuda` came from the host, make sure targets/x86_64-linux/lib is present (tarball installs it under `targets/`). Also check `readlink -f /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libnvrtc.so*`.

lina: `ldd` shows `libnvrtc.so => not found`. I installed CUDA via the runfile on the VM, but maybe I missed a component.

ben: try installing the toolkit deb (preferred) or copy the `targets/x86_64-linux/lib/libnvrtc.so*` into lib64 and run `sudo ldconfig`. Avoid ad-hoc symlinks long-term. Also add `-DCMAKE_BUILD_RPATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64` when invoking cmake to bake rpath.

lina: thanks. small follow-up: I'm building inside conda env with gcc-12. CI uses gcc-11. Could that matter?

anya: yes, nvcc and gcc mismatch can produce odd link errors. We recommend using the internal dev image pinned to gcc-11: `redwood/dev:cuda-12.1-gcc11`. If you need a GPU VM with that image, ping infra.

infra-bot: infra-bot: to request a pre-baked onboarding VM, post in #eng-infra with `gpu-dev-onboard`, your username, and desired CUDA (default: 12.1).

lina: I don't have access to the internal image yet. As a workaround I copied libnvrtc from targets into lib64 and re-ran ldconfig; link moved past nvrtc but now errors refer to `libdevice` relocation messages at runtime.

ben: that suggests ABI mismatch between the device library and the nvcc runtime. Reinstall full toolkit matching the nvcc version or use the docker image. Also confirm `nvcc --version` inside the build environment and `nvidia-smi` on the host driver; avoid mixing CUDA 12.2 toolkit with a 12.1 dev image.

lina: got it. I'll request the infra VM and switch to the pinned docker image. If I still hit problems, can someone pair?

anya: ping me, happy to pair for the initial setup. Congrats on joining! :tada:

lina: thanks all, will update here after the infra VM is provisioned. :thumbsup:
